fields.statement: At 6d5ec8e2 built rhiza (go build -trimpath) and ran its real daemon (paused, rhiza.web.port 18777) in a scratch clone holding copies of this repo's 100 run journals. GET /runs answered 200: a Recent group of 50 rows newest first (Fix The daemon never reaps its, Web UI Roadmap pages, ...), each linking to /runs/<id>, with its change set title, workflow (ship-change/plan), state pill, current step (build/build) and start time (Nov 6 01:13), no ID text; the list section declares data-rz-events=run and /fragments/runs. With one older run's lock held by flock, /fragments/runs put it alone under Live (running pill) before Recent. Appending to a journal emitted event: run on /events.

At 6d5ec8e2 with the built rhiza's real daemon web UI over copied real run journals: GET /runs/<id> answered 404 for every run (a ship-change run, a plan run, a succeeded run) as well as for an unknown one, and /fragments/run-detail?run=<id> rendered No such run. GET /api/run.status through the same server answers 404 no read-only operation "run.status": run.status (internal/api/run.go:55) is not marked ReadOnly, so ReadOnlyHandler refuses it and runDetail maps the 404 to a page 404. The package tests pass only because they serve run.status from a fake API handler.

At 6d5ec8e2 with the built rhiza's real daemon web UI: /api/run.tail is served (200); /fragments/run-log?run=<plan run> rendered the driver log's last lines in the rz-term block (Live) matching the file's tail; a run with no log rendered No log / Only a run the daemon started headless has a driver log; appending two lines to the log emitted event: log with the run's id on /events and the fragment then showed both new lines. But the run's page itself (/runs/<id>) answers 404 for every run because run.status is not read-only, so no run page shows the tail.
